summary: Request: Immutable audit ledger delta export and SIEM backfill plan for 90-day retention
description:
Issue summary: Customer requests a reproducible, verifiable 'immutable audit ledger' export to support a 90-day SIEM backfill and ongoing delta deliveries. They require a plan showing how Redwood will: 1) produce an initial backfill bundle covering 2025-11-01 to present, 2) provide incremental delta exports (hourly) with deterministic ordering and checksums, 3) include pseudonymization for PII fields, and 4) deliver cryptographic proof (digest/hmac/x509-signed manifest) that the archive has not been tampered with.

Background: FinLedger is undergoing a regulatory audit and wants a vendor-provided backfill and a repeatable daily delta feed into their SIEM (Graylog). They need evidence for chain-of-custody and demonstrable immutability for ingestion into their compliance archive.

Requested deliverables: initial backfill (S3-compatible bundle or signed tarball), delta ingest endpoint or push schedule with manifest and checksums, field mapping document for SIEM ingestion (timestamp formats, tenant_id mapping, event_type normalization), PII redaction/pseudonymization description, and a short runbook for verification steps auditors will run.
impact: Customer audit start date: 2026-03-18. Without a timely deliverable they risk non-compliance findings. Current blocking: customer cannot finalize SIEM retention evidence. Business impact: enterprise contract renewal dependent on compliance deliverables.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requests export through support form. 2) Support ticket created and triaged. 3) Customer provided sample ingest spec but requires vendor-signed immutable proof. 4) Attempted export with existing S3 snapshot process but lacks signed manifest and delta sequencing to their spec.
expected_behavior: We provide: - A one-time backfill bundle containing ordered events (UTC canonical timestamps), an accompanying manifest with SHA-256 checksums per file, and an overall signed digest (x509). - Hourly delta feeds with sequence numbers and HMAC per payload. - Field mapping and pseudonymization report. - Verification steps and a contact for on-call engineering during auditor validation.
actual_behavior: Current automated snapshot produces un-signed archives and uses internal eventIDs that do not match customer's tenant-scoped ordering requirement. Delta feed exists but lacks stable sequence numbers and cryptographic manifests required by FinLedger. No existing runbook for auditor verification.
logs: support: initial_request: 2026-03-09T14:02Z - payload sample attached in customer portal (omitted). export_attempt: 2026-03-11T03:40Z - snapshot created: s3://redwood-exports/sup-72011/tmp-backfill-20260311.tar.gz (no manifest). connector: error: missing field 'tenant_hash' in exported schema mapping.csv
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Eng triage - audit-service can generate chronological snapshots, but manifest/signing currently lives in a different pipeline (archive-service).

2026-03-12: Confirmed: delta feed is available via /internal/delta but sequence numbers are monotonic per pod, not globally ordered. Will need router-level sequence assignment or include ledger sequence field in exporter.

2026-03-13: Security: x509 signing routine exists in key-management service; recommend HSM-backed signing for enterprise deliverable. Need approval from Product for privileged operation for customer export.

Hypothesis: combining archive-service snapshot + kinesis-ordered replay will satisfy ordering and allow signed manifest generation. Backfill window estimated size ~120 GB compressed for 90 days for this tenant.

notes_for_engineering: - Aim for deterministic ordering field 'ledger_seq' that is monotonic across the tenant; include event_origin metadata. - Use SHA-256 per chunk and sign manifest via HSM-backed key. - Provide a small verification script (python) that auditors can run to validate checksums and signatures.
auditor_verification_instructions: 1) Download all files listed in manifest. 2) Verify SHA-256 of each file matches manifest entries. 3) Verify overall signed digest using provided x509 certificate. 4) Replay events into test SIEM using 'ledger_seq' ordering and confirm event counts. (Provide contact: miguel.ortega@redwood.ai)
customer_acceptance_criteria: - Backfill bundle delivered and signed. - Hourly delta feed with 'ledger_seq' and HMAC delivered and demonstrably consumable by customer's Graylog. - Field mapping and pseudonymization report provided. - Auditors can successfully validate checksums and signature in a staging replay test.
